headline: Trump is giving Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million fraud bounty program
summary: The Trump administration announced a new $25 million fraud bounty program. Right-wing YouTuber Nick Shirley received $10,000 as the program's first payout. Shirley's viral video from December 2025 alleged fraud at Minnesota daycares.

headline: Google’s more personalized Gemini AI is heading to your car
summary: Google is integrating its personalized Gemini AI into Android Auto and cars with Google built-in. Gemini will access user data from Google apps like Gmail, Calendar, and Maps. This allows for context-aware assistance, such as providing flight status updates while driving.

headline: Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla and SpaceX are exploring a potential merger. Special committees, composed of independent directors, have been formed to discuss the possibility. The discussions were initiated at the request of shareholders.

headline: SpaceX will try catching Starship and its booster for first time, Musk says
summary: SpaceX plans to attempt catching Starship and its booster next month. The goal is to achieve full recovery of the entire orbital launch system. Success would mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch vehicle in history.

headline: Mel Brooks Insisted on Shooting His Scenes for Spaceballs: The New One Before the Rest of the Cast
summary: Comedy legend Mel Brooks filmed his scenes for "Spaceballs: The New One" first. The centenarian director wanted to ensure his character, Yogurt, was included. This move was a precaution in case he passed away during production.

headline: It Looks Like GTA 6's Beer Brands Are About to Become Real
summary: Rockstar Games appears poised to launch real-life beer brands. These brands are prominently featured within the upcoming video game, GTA 6. This suggests an expansion of the game's universe into consumer merchandise.

headline: Greta Gerwig Reportedly Clashed With Netflix Film Boss Over Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew
summary: Greta Gerwig reportedly had a bitter falling out with Netflix's former head of film, Dan Lin. The dispute centered on her upcoming movie, "Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew." The clash highlights potential creative differences during the film's development.

headline: Police Confirm Nearly $1 Million Worth of Trading Cards Stolen in PSA FedEx Truck Heist
summary: Police confirmed that nearly $1 million worth of collectible trading cards were stolen. The heist occurred from a FedEx truck outside PSA’s Santa Ana headquarters. The estimated value of the stolen cards is over $963,000.

headline: Two men re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iran intelligence after RAF Fairford incident
summary: Two men have been re-arrested on suspicion of assisting Iranian intelligence. The re-arrests follow an incident at RAF Fairford. UK Counter Terrorism Policing considers Iranian state involvement "highly likely."

headline: Zelensky says US intelligence sharing 'works now' after talks with Trump envoy in Oslo
summary: President Zelensky affirmed that US intelligence sharing with Ukraine is now effective. This positive update follows recent talks with a Trump envoy in Oslo. Ukraine had previously accused the US of withholding intelligence, a claim denied by Washington.

headline: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds
summary: A Covid inquiry report found government failings significantly contributed to the rapid spread in care homes. Key criticisms include a severe lack of personal protective equipment (PPE). The inquiry also highlighted problematic patient discharges from hospitals into care facilities.

headline: BBC Three, BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra broadcast channels to close
summary: The BBC announced the closure of broadcast channels BBC Three, BBC Scotland, and Radio 4 Extra. These closures are part of a broader corporate strategy to save £500 million. The corporation aims to achieve these substantial savings over two years.
